- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–3% dampening factor if sentiment changes abruptly within 3–5 days prior.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 10-day smoothing or ignore sentiment spikes >0.75 for 3–5 days.
